CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.tooltip: Gross emissions from territorial deforestation. Estimates are based on the total removal of the biomass stored in the native vegetation, including above and below ground biomass, litter and deadwood.
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.long_description: Gross greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from territorial  deforestation, expressed in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent (t CO₂-eq) are determined by calculating the emissions resulting from the removal (land conversion) of native vegetation carbon stocks. Carbon stocks include the above and below ground biomass including necromass. The carbon stocks are based on the values provided by SEEG v12 (SEEG, 2024). Carbon is converted into CO₂-eq by multiplying the values by 3.67, based on the ratio between the molecular weight of C and CO₂.
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.citation: Lathuillière, M. J., Suavet, C., Biddle, H., Su, N., Prada Moro, Y., Carvalho, T., & Ribeiro, V. (2022). Brazil soy supply chain (2004-2022) (Version 2.6) [Data set]. Trase. https://doi.org/10.48650/DCE3-JJ97

PASTURE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.tooltip: Pasture deforestation is the amount of deforestation across a five-year allocation period that is converted to pasture. To calculate it, we overlapped the annual pasture maps from MapBiomas with the annual territorial deforestation five years prior to the target year for pasture, including the year the pasture was detected.
PASTURE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.long_description: Pasture deforestation is quantified as the total area of deforestation converted to pasture within a five-year allocation period. We calculate this by spatially overlapping annual pasture maps from MapBiomas with annual territorial deforestation data. This analysis identifies all deforestation that occurred within the five years prior to, and including, the year pasture was detected, yielding a cumulative estimate of deforestation linked to pasture land use. The territorial deforestation data is a composite dataset, integrating information from Prodes Amazon (INPE, 2025), Prodes Cerrado (INPE, 2025), and MapBiomas deforestation (MapBiomas, 2025; Souza et al., 2020) data for all other biomes.
PASTURE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.data_source: Prodes Amazon (INPE, 2025)\n Prodes Cerrado (INPE, 2025)\n Mapbiomas Collection 10 (MapBiomas, 2025; Souza et al., 2020)
PASTURE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.citation: zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J., Suavet, C., Biddle, H., Su, N., Prada Moro, Y., Ribeiro, V., Carvalho, T., & Lathuilliere, M. (2025). Brazil beef supply chain 2010–2017 and 2019–2023 (Version 2.2) [Data set]. Trase.

CATTLE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.tooltip: Cattle deforestation is the amount of deforestation associated with the production of beef for a given year. Cattle deforestation builds on pasture deforestation and assumes a 5 year life cycle from birth to slaughter, accounting for the average pasture deforestation during the 5 year lifespan.
CATTLE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.long_description: Cattle deforestation estimates the amount of deforestation associated with the production of beef for a given year. Cattle deforestation combines the area deforested for pastures and cattle production, assuming a 5 year life cycle from birth to slaughter, accounting for the average pasture deforestation during the 5 year lifespan.
CATTLE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.citation: zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J., Suavet, C., Biddle, H., Su, N., Prada Moro, Y., Ribeiro, V., Carvalho, T., & Lathuilliere, M. (2025). Brazil beef supply chain 2010–2017 and 2019–2023 (Version 2.2) [Data set]. Trase.

CATTLE_DEFORESTATION_PER_TN_5_YEAR_TOTAL.tooltip: Cattle deforestation per ton is the pasture deforestation associated with the full production life-cycle of beef for a given year, expressed in hectares deforested per ton of carcass. We assume a 5 year life cycle from birth to slaughter accounting for average production and pasture deforestation during the life cycle.
CATTLE_DEFORESTATION_PER_TN_5_YEAR_TOTAL.long_description: Cattle deforestation per ton estimates the amount of deforestation associated with the production of beef for a given year, expressed in hectares deforested per ton of carcass. Cattle assumes a 5 year life cycle from birth to slaughter accounting for the average production and pasture deforestation during the life cycle.
CATTLE_DEFORESTATION_PER_TN_5_YEAR_TOTAL.citation: zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J., Suavet, C., Biddle, H., Su, N., Prada Moro, Y., Ribeiro, V., Carvalho, T., & Lathuilliere, M. (2025). Brazil beef supply chain 2010–2017 and 2019–2023 (Version 2.2) [Data set]. Trase.

CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_PASTURE_DEFORESTATIO.tooltip: Gross CO₂-eq emissions from pasture deforestation (using a 5-year allocation period), estimate emissions from the loss of the native vegetation biomass (above- and below-ground, litter, and deadwood; excluding soil carbon).
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_PASTURE_DEFORESTATIO.long_description: Gross greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from pasture deforestation, expressed in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent (t CO₂-eq), are determined by calculating the emissions resulting from the removal (land conversion) of native vegetation carbon stocks. Carbon stocks include the above and below ground biomass including necromass. The carbon stocks are based on the values provided by SEEG v12 (SEEG, 2024). Carbon is converted into CO₂-eq by multiplying the values by 3.67, based on the ratio between the molecular weight of C and CO₂.
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_PASTURE_DEFORESTATIO.citation: zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J., Suavet, C., Biddle, H., Su, N., Prada Moro, Y., Ribeiro, V., Carvalho, T., & Lathuilliere, M. (2025). Brazil beef supply chain 2010–2017 and 2019–2023 (Version 2.2) [Data set]. Trase.

CO2_NET_EMISSIONS_PASTURE_DEFORESTATION_.tooltip: Net CO₂-eq emissions attributable to pasture deforestation (using a 5-year allocation period). Estimates are based on the difference between the biomass stored in the native vegetation biomass (above- and below-ground, litter, and deadwood; excluding soil carbon).
CO2_NET_EMISSIONS_PASTURE_DEFORESTATION_.long_description: Net greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from pasture deforestation, expressed in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent (t CO₂-eq), are determined by calculating the emissions resulting from the removal of native vegetation carbon stocks, due to deforestation for pasture, and the carbon stored in pasture. Carbon stocks include above and below ground biomass including necromass. Both the native vegetation and the pasture carbon stocks are based on estimates provided by SEEG v12 (SEEG, 2024). Carbon is converted into CO₂-eq by multiplying the values by 3.67, based on the ratio between the molecular weight of C and CO₂.
CO2_NET_EMISSIONS_PASTURE_DEFORESTATION_.citation: zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J., Suavet, C., Biddle, H., Su, N., Prada Moro, Y., Ribeiro, V., Carvalho, T., & Lathuilliere, M. (2025). Brazil beef supply chain 2010–2017 and 2019–2023 (Version 2.2) [Data set]. Trase.

CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_CATTLE_DEFORESTATION.long_description: Gross greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from cattle deforestation, expressed in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent (t CO₂-eq), are determined by calculating the emissions resulting from the removal of native vegetation carbon stocks. Carbon stocks include the above and below ground biomass including necromass. The carbon stocks are based on the values provided by SEEG v12 (SEEG, 2024). CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_CATTLE_DEFORESTATION.citation: zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J., Suavet, C., Biddle, H., Su, N., Prada Moro, Y., Ribeiro, V., Carvalho, T., & Lathuilliere, M. (2025). Brazil beef supply chain 2010–2017 and 2019–2023 (Version 2.2) [Data set]. Trase.

CO2_NET_EMISSIONS_CATTLE_DEFORESTATION_5.long_description: Net greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from cattle deforestation, expressed in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent (t CO₂-eq), are estimated based on the difference between the biomass stored in the native vegetation biomass before land conversion and the carbon stored in pastures. Carbon stocks include above and below ground biomass including necromass. Both the native vegetation and the pasture carbon stocks are based on estimates provided by SEEG v12 (SEEG, 2024). Carbon is converted into CO₂-eq by multiplying the values by 3.67, based on the ratio between the molecular weight of C and CO₂.
CO2_NET_EMISSIONS_CATTLE_DEFORESTATION_5.citation: zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J., Suavet, C., Biddle, H., Su, N., Prada Moro, Y., Ribeiro, V., Carvalho, T., & Lathuilliere, M. (2025). Brazil beef supply chain 2010–2017 and 2019–2023 (Version 2.2) [Data set]. Trase.

CO2_NET_EMISSIONS_CATTLE_DEFORESTATION_P.citation: zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J., Suavet, C., Biddle, H., Su, N., Prada Moro, Y., Ribeiro, V., Carvalho, T., & Lathuilliere, M. (2025). Brazil beef supply chain 2010–2017 and 2019–2023 (Version 2.2) [Data set]. Trase.

CATTLE_TN.tooltip: Estimated cattle production in tonnes of carcass.

Carcass weight is derived from IBGE carcass weights (IBGE, 2025)

SOY_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.tooltip: Soy deforestation is the amount of deforestation across a five-year allocation period that is converted to soy. To calculate it, we overlapped the annual soy maps from GLAD, in the southern hemisphere, and Mapbiomas soy, for the northern hemisphere with the annual territorial deforestation up to six years prior to the soy harvest, excluding the time from planting to harvest.
SOY_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.long_description: Soy deforestation is quantified as the total area of deforestation converted to soy within a five-year allocation period accounting for a one year lag between planting and harvest. We calculate this by spatially overlapping territorial deforestation and annual soy maps from GLAD in the southern hemisphere (Song et al., 2021) and Mapbiomas soy in the northern hemisphere (MapBiomas, 2025; Souza et al., 2020). This analysis identifies all deforestation that occurred within the five years prior to planting, yielding a cumulative estimate of deforestation linked to soy production. The territorial deforestation data is a composite dataset, integrating information from Prodes Amazon (INPE, 2025), Prodes Cerrado (INPE, 2025), and MapBiomas deforestation (MapBiomas, 2025; Souza et al., 2020) data for all other biomes.

CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.tooltip: Gross emissions from territorial deforestation. Estimates are based on the total removal of the biomass stored in the native vegetation, including above and below ground biomass, litter and deadwood.
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.long_description: Gross greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from territorial  deforestation, expressed in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent (t CO₂-eq) are determined by calculating the emissions resulting from the removal (land conversion) of native vegetation carbon stocks. Carbon stocks include the above and below ground biomass including necromass. The carbon stocks are based on the values provided by SEEG v12 (SEEG, 2024). Carbon is converted into CO₂-eq by multiplying the values by 3.67, based on the ratio between the molecular weight of C and CO₂.

PASTURE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.tooltip: Pasture deforestation is the amount of deforestation across a five-year allocation period that is converted to pasture. To calculate it, we overlapped the annual pasture maps from MapBiomas with the annual territorial deforestation five years prior to the target year for pasture, including the year the pasture was detected.
PASTURE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.long_description: Pasture deforestation is quantified as the total area of deforestation converted to pasture within a five-year allocation period. We calculate this by spatially overlapping annual pasture maps from MapBiomas with annual territorial deforestation data. This analysis identifies all deforestation that occurred within the five years prior to, and including, the year pasture was detected, yielding a cumulative estimate of deforestation linked to pasture land use. The territorial deforestation data is a composite dataset, integrating information from Prodes Amazon (INPE, 2025), Prodes Cerrado (INPE, 2025), and MapBiomas deforestation (MapBiomas, 2025; Souza et al., 2020) data for all other biomes.
PASTURE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.data_source: Prodes Amazon (INPE, 2025)\n Prodes Cerrado (INPE, 2025)\n Mapbiomas Collection 10 (MapBiomas, 2025; Souza et al., 2020)
PASTURE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.citation: zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J., Suavet, C., Biddle, H., Su, N., Prada Moro, Y., Ribeiro, V., Carvalho, T., & Lathuilliere, M. (2025). Brazil beef supply chain 2010–2017 and 2019–2023 (Version 2.2) [Data set]. Trase.

CATTLE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.tooltip: Cattle deforestation is the amount of deforestation associated with the production of beef for a given year. CATTLE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.long_description: Cattle deforestation estimates the amount of deforestation associated with the production of beef for a given year. Cattle deforestation combines the area deforested for pastures and cattle production, assuming a 5 year life cycle from birth to slaughter, accounting for the average pasture deforestation during the 5 year lifespan.

CATTLE_DEFORESTATION_PER_TN_5_YEAR_TOTAL.tooltip: Cattle deforestation per ton is the pasture deforestation associated with the full production life-cycle of beef for a given year, expressed in hectares deforested per ton of carcass. We assume a 5 year life cycle from birth to slaughter accounting for average production and pasture deforestation during the life cycle.
CATTLE_DEFORESTATION_PER_TN_5_YEAR_TOTAL.long_description: Cattle deforestation per ton estimates the amount of deforestation associated with the production of beef for a given year, expressed in hectares deforested per ton of carcass. Cattle assumes a 5 year life cycle from birth to slaughter accounting for the average production and pasture deforestation during the life cycle.

CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_PASTURE_DEFORESTATIO.long_description: Gross greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from pasture deforestation, expressed in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent (t CO₂-eq), are determined by calculating the emissions resulting from the removal (land conversion) of native vegetation carbon stocks. Carbon is converted into CO₂-eq by multiplying the values by 3.67, based on the ratio between the molecular weight of C and CO₂.

CO2_NET_EMISSIONS_PASTURE_DEFORESTATION_.tooltip: Net CO₂-eq emissions attributable to pasture deforestation (using a 5-year allocation period). CO2_NET_EMISSIONS_PASTURE_DEFORESTATION_.long_description: Net greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from pasture deforestation, expressed in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent (t CO₂-eq), are determined by calculating the emissions resulting from the removal of native vegetation carbon stocks, due to deforestation for pasture, and the carbon stored in pasture. Carbon stocks include above and below ground biomass including necromass. Both the native vegetation and the pasture carbon stocks are based on estimates provided by SEEG v12 (SEEG, 2024). Carbon is converted into CO₂-eq by multiplying the values by 3.67, based on the ratio between the molecular weight of C and CO₂.

CATTLE_TN.tooltip: Estimated cattle production in tonnes of carcass.
CATTLE_TN.long_description: Cattle production (ton carcass) per municipality, per year, is calculated as: herd size (per muni/yr) * slaughter rate (per state/yr) * carcass weight (per state/yr). Herd size is derived from IBGE cattle heads (IBGE, 2025), slaughter rate: extrapolates Annualpec slaughter data (IEG & FNP, 2019), based on IBGE slaughter data and corrected for SIGSIF animal movements (MAPA, 2019). Carcass weight is derived from IBGE carcass weights (IBGE, 2025)
CATTLE_TN.data_source:
IBGE cattle herd size (IBGE, 2025)
Annualpec slaughter rate (IEG & FNP, 2019)
IBGE slaughter rate (IBGE, 2025)
SIGSIF animal movement (MAPA, 2019)
IBGE carcass weight  (IBGE, 2025)

SOY_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.tooltip: Soy deforestation is the amount of deforestation across a five-year allocation period that is converted to soy. To calculate it, we overlapped the annual soy maps from GLAD, in the southern hemisphere, and Mapbiomas soy, for the northern hemisphere with the annual territorial deforestation up to six years prior to the soy harvest, excluding the time from planting to harvest.
SOY_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.long_description: Soy deforestation is quantified as the total area of deforestation converted to soy within a five-year allocation period accounting for a one year lag between planting and harvest. We calculate this by spatially overlapping territorial deforestation and annual soy maps from GLAD in the southern hemisphere (Song et al., 2021) and Mapbiomas soy in the northern hemisphere (MapBiomas, 2025; Souza et al., 2020). This analysis identifies all deforestation that occurred within the five years prior to planting, yielding a cumulative estimate of deforestation linked to soy production. The territorial deforestation data is a composite dataset, integrating information from Prodes Amazon (INPE, 2025), Prodes Cerrado (INPE, 2025), and MapBiomas deforestation (MapBiomas, 2025; Souza et al., 2020) data for all other biomes.

Prodes Amazon (INPE, 2025)
Prodes Cerrado (INPE, 2025)
Mapbiomas Collection 10 (MapBiomas, 2025; Souza et al., 2020)

CO2_NET_EMISSIONS_PASTURE_DEFORESTATION_.long_description: Net greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from pasture deforestation, expressed in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent (t CO₂-eq), are determined by calculating the emissions resulting from the removal of native vegetation carbon stocks, due to deforestation for pasture, and the carbon stored in pasture. Carbon stocks include above and below ground biomass including necromass. Both the native vegetation and the pasture carbon stocks are based on estimates provided by SEEG v12 (SEEG, 2024). Carbon is converted into CO₂-eq by multiplying the values by 3.67, based on the ratio between the molecular weight of C and CO₂.

CATTLE_TN.tooltip: Estimated cattle production in tonnes of carcass.
CATTLE_TN.long_description: Cattle production (ton carcass) per municipality, per year, is calculated as: herd size (per muni/yr) * slaughter rate (per state/yr) * carcass weight (per state/yr). Herd size is derived from IBGE cattle heads (IBGE, 2025), slaughter rate: extrapolates Annualpec slaughter data (IEG & FNP, 2019), based on IBGE slaughter data and corrected for SIGSIF animal movements (MAPA, 2019). Carcass weight is derived from IBGE carcass weights (IBGE, 2025)
CATTLE_TN.data_source:
IBGE cattle herd size (IBGE, 2025)
Annualpec slaughter rate (IEG & FNP, 2019)
IBGE slaughter rate (IBGE, 2025)
SIGSIF animal movement (MAPA, 2019)
IBGE carcass weight  (IBGE, 2025)
CATTLE_TN.citation: zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J., Suavet, C., Biddle, H., Su, N., Prada Moro, Y., Ribeiro, V., Carvalho, T., & Lathuilliere, M. (2025). Brazil beef supply chain 2010–2017 and 2019–2023 (Version 2.2) [Data set]. Trase.

SOY_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.tooltip: Soy deforestation is the amount of deforestation across a five-year allocation period that is converted to soy. To calculate it, we overlapped the annual soy maps from GLAD, in the southern hemisphere, and Mapbiomas soy, for the northern hemisphere with the annual territorial deforestation up to six years prior to the soy harvest, excluding the time from planting to harvest.
SOY_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.long_description: Soy deforestation is quantified as the total area of deforestation converted to soy within a five-year allocation period accounting for a one year lag between planting and harvest. We calculate this by spatially overlapping territorial deforestation and annual soy maps from GLAD in the southern hemisphere (Song et al., 2021) and Mapbiomas soy in the northern hemisphere (MapBiomas, 2025; Souza et al., 2020). This analysis identifies all deforestation that occurred within the five years prior to planting, yielding a cumulative estimate of deforestation linked to soy production. The territorial deforestation data is a composite dataset, integrating information from Prodes Amazon (INPE, 2025), Prodes Cerrado (INPE, 2025), and MapBiomas deforestation (MapBiomas, 2025; Souza et al., 2020) data for all other biomes.
SOY_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.data_source:
GLAD (Song et al., 2021)
Prodes Amazon (INPE, 2025)
Prodes Cerrado (INPE, 2025)
Mapbiomas Collection 10 (MapBiomas, 2025; Souza et al., 2020)
SOY_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.citation: Lathuillière, M. J., Suavet, C., Biddle, H., Su, N., Prada Moro, Y., Carvalho, T., & Ribeiro, V. (2022). Brazil soy supply chain (2004-2022) (Version 2.6) [Data set]. Trase.

PASTURE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.tooltip: Pasture deforestation is the amount of deforestation across a five-year allocation period that is converted to pasture. To calculate it, we overlapped the annual pasture maps from MapBiomas with the annual territorial deforestation five years prior to the target year for pasture, including the year the pasture was detected.
PASTURE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.long_description: Pasture deforestation is quantified as the total area of deforestation converted to pasture within a five-year allocation period. We calculate this by spatially overlapping annual pasture maps from MapBiomas with annual territorial deforestation data. This analysis identifies all deforestation that occurred within the five years prior to, and including, the year pasture was detected, yielding a cumulative estimate of deforestation linked to pasture land use. The territorial deforestation data is a composite dataset, integrating information from Prodes Amazon (INPE, 2025), Prodes Cerrado (INPE, 2025), and MapBiomas deforestation (MapBiomas, 2025; Souza et al., 2020) data for all other biomes.

CATTLE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.tooltip: Cattle deforestation is the amount of deforestation associated with the production of beef for a given year. CATTLE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.long_description: Cattle deforestation estimates the amount of deforestation associated with the production of beef for a given year. CATTLE_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.citation: zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J., Suavet, C., Biddle, H., Su, N., Prada Moro, Y., Ribeiro, V., Carvalho, T., & Lathuilliere, M. (2025). Brazil beef supply chain 2010–2017 and 2019–2023 (Version 2.2) [Data set]. Trase.

CATTLE_TN.tooltip: Estimated cattle production in tonnes of carcass.
CATTLE_TN.long_description: Cattle production (ton carcass) per municipality, per year, is calculated as: herd size (per muni/yr) * slaughter rate (per state/yr) * carcass weight (per state/yr). Herd size is derived from IBGE cattle heads (IBGE, 2025), slaughter rate: extrapolates Annualpec slaughter data (IEG & FNP, 2019), based on IBGE slaughter data and corrected for SIGSIF animal movements (MAPA, 2019). Carcass weight is derived from IBGE carcass weights (IBGE, 2025)
CATTLE_TN.data_source:
IBGE cattle herd size (IBGE, 2025)
Annualpec slaughter rate (IEG & FNP, 2019)
IBGE slaughter rate (IBGE, 2025)
SIGSIF animal movement (MAPA, 2019)
IBGE carcass weight  (IBGE, 2025)

SOY_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.tooltip: Soy deforestation is the amount of deforestation across a five-year allocation period that is converted to soy. To calculate it, we overlapped the annual soy maps from GLAD, in the southern hemisphere, and Mapbiomas soy, for the northern hemisphere with the annual territorial deforestation up to six years prior to the soy harvest, excluding the time from planting to harvest.
SOY_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.long_description: Soy deforestation is quantified as the total area of deforestation converted to soy within a five-year allocation period accounting for a one year lag between planting and harvest. We calculate this by spatially overlapping territorial deforestation and annual soy maps from GLAD in the southern hemisphere (Song et al., 2021) and Mapbiomas soy in the northern hemisphere (MapBiomas, 2025; Souza et al., 2020). This analysis identifies all deforestation that occurred within the five years prior to planting, yielding a cumulative estimate of deforestation linked to soy production. The territorial deforestation data is a composite dataset, integrating information from Prodes Amazon (INPE, 2025), Prodes Cerrado (INPE, 2025), and MapBiomas deforestation (MapBiomas, 2025; Souza et al., 2020) data for all other biomes.
SOY_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.data_source:
GLAD (Song et al., 2021)
Prodes Amazon (INPE, 2025)
Prodes Cerrado (INPE, 2025)
Mapbiomas Collection 10 (MapBiomas, 2025; Souza et al., 2020)
SOY_DEFORESTATION_5_YEAR_TOTAL.citation: Lathuillière, M. J., Suavet, C., Biddle, H., Su, N., Prada Moro, Y., Carvalho, T., & Ribeiro, V. (2022). Brazil soy supply chain (2004-2022) (Version 2.6) [Data set]. Trase.

CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_SOY_DEFORESTATION_5_.tooltip: Gross CO₂-eq emissions from soy deforestation (using a 5-year allocation period), estimate emissions from the loss of the native vegetation biomass, including above- and below-ground, litter, and deadwood, while excluding soil carbon.
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_SOY_DEFORESTATION_5_.long_description: Gross greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from soy deforestation, expressed in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent (t CO₂-eq) are determined by calculating the emissions resulting from the removal (land conversion) of native vegetation carbon stocks. Carbon stocks include the above and below ground biomass including necromass. The carbon stocks are based on the values provided by SEEG v12 (SEEG, 2024). Carbon is converted into CO₂-eq by multiplying the values by 3.67, based on the ratio between the molecular weight of C and CO₂.
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_SOY_DEFORESTATION_5_.citation: Lathuillière, M. J., Suavet, C., Biddle, H., Su, N., Prada Moro, Y., Carvalho, T., & Ribeiro, V. (2022). Brazil soy supply chain (2004-2022) (Version 2.6) [Data set]. Trase.

TERRITORIAL_DEFORESTATION.tooltip: Deforestation of undisturbed Tropical Moist Forest derived from EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Note that values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
TERRITORIAL_DEFORESTATION.long_description: Deforestation maps were derived from the European Commission's Joint Research Centre 's TMF dataset Version 1 from 2023 (Vancutsem et al., 2021) using 41 years of Landsat time series at 30 metre spatial resolution and aggregated at department level. Deforestation refers to the year of change in land cover, from undisturbed or degraded forest (see above) to non-forest (Vancutsem et al., 2021).
TERRITORIAL_DEFORESTATION.data_source: JRC Tropical Moist Forest (AnnualChanges layer)\n(Vancutsem et al., 2021)
TERRITORIAL_DEFORESTATION.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

TERRITORIAL_DEGRADATION.tooltip: Degradation of Tropical Moist Forest derived from EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Note that values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
TERRITORIAL_DEGRADATION.long_description: Maps of degraded forest were derived from the European Commission's Joint Research Centre's TMF dataset Version 1 from 2023  (Vancutsem et al., 2021) using 41 years of Landsat time series at 30 metre spatial resolution and aggregated at department level. Forest degradation was defined as a disturbance in the tree cover canopy  visible from space over a short time period (< 2.5 years). A 'forest degradation' pixel remains forested land; i.e.,  covered by existing or regrowing trees, whereas a 'deforestation' pixel leads to the long-term (visible > 2.5 years) conversion into non-forested land  (Vancutsem et al., 2021).
TERRITORIAL_DEGRADATION.data_source: JRC Tropical Moist Forest (AnnualChanges layer)\n(Vancutsem et al., 2021)
TERRITORIAL_DEGRADATION.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

TERRITORIAL_UNDISTURBED_FOREST.tooltip: Area of undisturbed Tropical Moist Forest derived from EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Note that values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
TERRITORIAL_UNDISTURBED_FOREST.long_description: Undisturbed forest maps were derived from the European Commission's Joint Research Centre's forest cover change in tropical moist forests (TMF) dataset Version 1 from 2023 (Vancutsem et al., 2021) using 41 years of Landsat time series at 30 metre spatial resolution and aggregated at department level. Undisturbed forest was defined as a closed evergreen or semi-evergreen forest without any disturbance observed over the full Landsat historical dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021).
TERRITORIAL_UNDISTURBED_FOREST.data_source: JRC Tropical Moist Forest (AnnualChanges layer)\n(Vancutsem et al., 2021)
TERRITORIAL_UNDISTURBED_FOREST.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.display_name: Gross greenhouse gas emissions from deforestation
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.tooltip: Gross CO₂-eq. emissions from deforestation, estimated from the loss of above- and below-ground biomass (excluding soil carbon) from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Carbon stocks were converted to CO₂-eq. by multiplying by 3.67. Note that values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.long_description: Gross (greenhouse gas) emissions from territorial deforestation (tonnes of CO2-eq) were calculated by estimating the maximum CO2-eq potentially emitted due to the full removal of the biomass as a result of territorial deforestation, estimated in a given year. This metric is calculated by multiplying the area of territorial deforestation by an estimate of the carbon stock contained in each hectare of converted land. Carbon stocks represent the total carbon stored in above- and below-ground biomass, but does not include carbon stocks in the soil. We create local estimates of biomass density (carbon stocks per hectare) using data from (Soto-Navarro et al., 2020). Carbon is converted into CO₂-eq emissions by multiplying by a factor of 44/12 ( or 3.67), based on the ratio between the molecular weight of C and CO₂ following (Pachauri et al., 2015).
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.data_source: (Pachauri et al., 2015; Soto-Navarro et al., 2020; Vancutsem C. et al., 2020)
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_DEFORESTATION_15_YEARS_TOTAL.tooltip: Cocoa deforestation is the amount of deforestation within a 15-year allocation period that is converted to cocoa plantations. To calculate it, we overlapped the cocoa area map from (Kalischek et al., 2023) (representing cocoa plantations in 2019 to 2021) with the annual loss of undisturbed Tropical Moist Forests from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021), applying a four-year lag between deforestation and first potential harvest to reflect the time from planting to harvest. Note that this does not account for cocoa expansion after 2021, and values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
COCOA_DEFORESTATION_15_YEARS_TOTAL.long_description: This metric estimates the amount of undisturbed forest converted to cocoa plantations over a 15 year period that is associated with cocoa production and exports in a selected year and department (Renier et al., 2023; Vancutsem et al., 2021). To estimate the deforestation associated with cocoa exports in a given year, we apply: a) a four-year lag between cocoa planting and the first harvest, reflecting the time required for plantations to become productive, and b) a 15-year allocation period over which plantations may contribute to traded cocoa volumes. Cocoa deforestation in 2021 is therefore calculated as the area of undisturbed forest converted to cocoa plantations between 2002 and 2017 at the location of cocoa production (Kalischek et al., 2023).
COCOA_DEFORESTATION_15_YEARS_TOTAL.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_DEFORESTATION_ANNUAL.tooltip: Annual deforestation embedded in cocoa harvest represents the area of forest loss associated with cocoa harvested in the current year, accounting for a four-year lag between land clearing and production.
COCOA_DEFORESTATION_ANNUAL.long_description: This metric estimates the annual amount of undisturbed forest converted to cocoa plantations that is associated with cocoa production and exports in a selected year and department (Renier et al., 2023; Vancutsem et al., 2021). To estimate the deforestation associated with cocoa exports in a given year, we apply a four-year lag between cocoa planting and the first harvest, reflecting the time required for plantations to become productive. Cocoa deforestation in 2021 is therefore calculated as the area of undisturbed forest converted to cocoa plantations in 2017 at the location of cocoa production (Kalischek et al., 2023).
COCOA_DEFORESTATION_ANNUAL.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_15_YEARS_TOTAL.tooltip: Gross CO₂-equivalent emissions from cocoa deforestation (15-year allocation period, 4-year lag), estimated from the loss of above- and below-ground biomass (excluding soil carbon). Carbon stocks were converted to CO₂-equivalent by multiplying by 3.67. To calculate above and belowground biomass loss, we overlapped the cocoa area map from (Kalischek et al., 2023) (representing cocoa plantations in 2019 to 2021) with the loss of undisturbed Tropical Moist Forests from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021), applying a four-year lag between deforestation and first potential harvest to reflect the time from planting to harvest. Note that values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_15_YEARS_TOTAL.long_description: This metric estimates the gross greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions associated with cocoa-driven deforestation over a 15-year period expressed in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent, and embedded in cocoa trade.  Emissions are calculated from the carbon stored in above- and below-ground biomass lost when undisturbed forest is deforested (excl. degradation) (Vancutsem et al., 2021) and converted to cocoa plantations (Kalischek et al., 2023), excluding soil carbon. To link emissions to cocoa exports, the metric applies a four-year lag between deforestation and the first cocoa harvest, reflecting the time required for cocoa trees to become productive, and allocates impacts over a 15-year production period. Carbon stock estimates are based on local biomass density data (Soto-Navarro et al., 2020) and converted to CO₂-equivalent using a factor of 3.67 (Pachauri et al., 2015). Estimates are based on cocoa plantation maps (Kalischek et al., 2023) and tropical forest loss data from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Values for recent years may change in future dataset updates as recent forest disturbance is reclassified over time.
COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_15_YEARS_TOTAL.data_source: (Kalischek et al., 2023; Pachauri et al., 2015; Soto-Navarro et al., 2020; Vancutsem et al., 2021)
COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_15_YEARS_TOTAL.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_ANNUAL.display_name: Gross emissions from annual cocoa deforestation
COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_ANNUAL.tooltip: Annual gross CO₂-equivalent emissions embedded in cocoa harvest were estimated from the loss of above- and below-ground biomass (excluding soil carbon). Carbon stocks were converted to CO₂-equivalent by multiplying by 3.67. To calculate above and belowground biomass loss, we overlapped the cocoa area map from (Kalischek et al., 2023) (representing cocoa plantations in 2019 to 2021) with the annual loss of undisturbed Tropical Moist Forests from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021).
COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_ANNUAL.long_description: This metric estimates the annual gross greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions associated with cocoa-driven deforestation expressed in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent and embedded in cocoa trade. Emissions are calculated from the carbon stored in above- and below-ground biomass lost when undisturbed forest is deforested (excl. degradation) (Vancutsem et al., 2021) and converted to cocoa plantations (Kalischek et al., 2023), excluding soil carbon. To link emissions to cocoa exports, the metric applies a four-year lag between deforestation and the first cocoa harvest, reflecting the time required for cocoa trees to become productive. Carbon stock estimates are based on local biomass density data (Soto-Navarro et al., 2020) and converted to CO₂-equivalent using a factor of 3.67 (Pachauri et al., 2015). Estimates are based on cocoa plantation maps  (Kalischek et al., 2023) and tropical forest loss data from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Values for recent years may change in future dataset updates as recent forest disturbance is reclassified over time.
COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_ANNUAL.data_source: (Kalischek et al., 2023; Pachauri et al., 2015; Soto-Navarro et al., 2020; Vancutsem et al., 2021)
COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_ANNUAL.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_NET_EMISSIONS_15_YEARS_TOTAL.tooltip: Net greenhouse gas emissions from cocoa deforestation (15-year allocation period, 4-year lag), were calculated as the difference between gross emissions from cocoa deforestation and sequestration in new cocoa plantations. To calculate above and belowground biomass loss, we overlapped the cocoa area map from (Kalischek et al., 2023) (representing cocoa plantations in 2019 to 2021) with the loss of undisturbed Tropical Moist Forests from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021), applying a four-year lag between deforestation and first potential harvest to reflect the time from planting to harvest. Note that values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
COCOA_NET_EMISSIONS_15_YEARS_TOTAL.long_description: This metric estimates the net greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions associated with cocoa-driven deforestation over a 15-year period expressed in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent, and embedded in cocoa trade. Net emissions are calculated as the difference between gross emissions from the loss of above- and below-ground biomass in undisturbed forests converted to cocoa plantations and carbon sequestration in cocoa and shade trees (Vervuurt et al., 2022), excluding soil carbon and forest degradation. To link emissions to cocoa exports, the metric applies a four-year lag between deforestation and the first cocoa harvest, and allocates impacts over a 15-year production period. Estimates are based on cocoa plantation maps (Kalischek et al., 2023) and tropical forest loss data from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Values for recent years may change in future dataset updates as recent forest disturbance is reclassified over time.
COCOA_NET_EMISSIONS_15_YEARS_TOTAL.data_source: (Kalischek et al., 2023; Soto-Navarro et al., 2020; Vancutsem et al., 2021; Vervuurt et al., 2022)

ZDC_TRADED_COTE_DIVOIRE_COCOA_PERC.display_name: Percentage of (total) cocoa that is exported under a zero deforestation commitment
ZDC_TRADED_COTE_DIVOIRE_COCOA_PERC.tooltip: Percentage of cocoa that is traded by traders with a zero deforestation commitment.
ZDC_TRADED_COTE_DIVOIRE_COCOA_PERC.long_description: Zero-deforestation commitments (ZDCs) were obtained from Global Canopy's research determining whether an exporting company group has a commitment or goal for zero deforestation in its cocoa supply chain in the year of cocoa export. A commitment is accepted as zero deforestation if an exporter group explicitly uses the phrases 'zero deforestation', 'zero conversion' in its sustainability goals, current policies, or if they have a policy (or target) for 100% certification where the certification is equivalent to a zero-deforestation standard. \nCommitments are reported as 'company commitment' (if the specific company has a ZDC), 'none' (if the company does not have one), or 'unknown' (if the company's ZDC position was not checked).
ZDC_TRADED_COTE_DIVOIRE_COCOA_PERC.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_TN.tooltip: Estimated production of cocoa based on national production data, cocoa areas, and cocoa suitability. Cocoa areas are from (Kalischek et al., 2023), based on satellite observations from 2019 to 2021.
COCOA_TN.long_description: This metric represents the estimated volume of cocoa production per department in Côte d'Ivoire in tonnes (t) per year. Department level cocoa production was calculated based on national production statistics, derived from the International Cocoa Organization (ICCO, 2023) and allocated to the individual departments weighted based on the cocoa area (see above) and relative cocoa suitability (Schroth et al., 2016) of plantations (Kalischek et al., 2023). Note, only the total cocoa production from ICCO varied between 2019 to 2022, while cocoa area and suitability were assumed stable for the whole period.
COCOA_TN.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_AREA.tooltip: Area of land used to grow cocoa from (Kalischek et al., 2023), based on satellite observations from 2019 to 2021.
COCOA_AREA.long_description: This metric represents the area of cocoa plantations in hectares (ha) for the years 2019–2021 per department in Côte d'Ivoire based on cocoa farming maps at 10 metre resolution. Cocoa maps were obtained from (Kalischek et al., 2023) and  based on Sentinel-2 images taken between January 2019 and December 2021. Because this dataset was based on images taken in a three year time span, Trase distributes the same cocoa area in all years, from 2019 to 2021.
COCOA_AREA.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_YIELD.tooltip: Average cocoa yield combining cocoa production (annual) and the cocoa area map from (Kalischek et al., 2023) (representing cocoa plantation in 2019 to 2021).
COCOA_YIELD.long_description: Cocoa yield per department was calculated based on cocoa area and cocoa production as tonnes produced per hectare (t/ha).
COCOA_YIELD.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

TERRITORIAL_DEFORESTATION.tooltip: Deforestation of undisturbed Tropical Moist Forest derived from EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Note that values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
TERRITORIAL_DEFORESTATION.long_description: Deforestation maps were derived from the European Commission's Joint Research Centre 's TMF dataset Version 1 from 2023 (Vancutsem et al., 2021) using 41 years of Landsat time series at 30 metre spatial resolution and aggregated at department level. Deforestation refers to the year of change in land cover, from undisturbed or degraded forest (see above) to non-forest (Vancutsem et al., 2021).
TERRITORIAL_DEFORESTATION.data_source: JRC Tropical Moist Forest (AnnualChanges layer)\n(Vancutsem et al., 2021)
TERRITORIAL_DEFORESTATION.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

TERRITORIAL_DEGRADATION.tooltip: Degradation of Tropical Moist Forest derived from EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Note that values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
TERRITORIAL_DEGRADATION.long_description: Maps of degraded forest were derived from the European Commission's Joint Research Centre's TMF dataset Version 1 from 2023  (Vancutsem et al., 2021) using 41 years of Landsat time series at 30 metre spatial resolution and aggregated at department level. Forest degradation was defined as a disturbance in the tree cover canopy  visible from space over a short time period (< 2.5 years). A 'forest degradation' pixel remains forested land; i.e.,  covered by existing or regrowing trees, whereas a 'deforestation' pixel leads to the long-term (visible > 2.5 years) conversion into non-forested land  (Vancutsem et al., 2021).
TERRITORIAL_DEGRADATION.data_source: JRC Tropical Moist Forest (AnnualChanges layer)\n(Vancutsem et al., 2021)
TERRITORIAL_DEGRADATION.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

TERRITORIAL_UNDISTURBED_FOREST.tooltip: Area of undisturbed Tropical Moist Forest derived from EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Note that values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
TERRITORIAL_UNDISTURBED_FOREST.long_description: Undisturbed forest maps were derived from the European Commission's Joint Research Centre's forest cover change in tropical moist forests (TMF) dataset Version 1 from 2023 (Vancutsem et al., 2021) using 41 years of Landsat time series at 30 metre spatial resolution and aggregated at department level. Undisturbed forest was defined as a closed evergreen or semi-evergreen forest without any disturbance observed over the full Landsat historical dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021).
TERRITORIAL_UNDISTURBED_FOREST.data_source: JRC Tropical Moist Forest (AnnualChanges layer)\n(Vancutsem et al., 2021)
TERRITORIAL_UNDISTURBED_FOREST.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.display_name: Gross greenhouse gas emissions from deforestation
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.tooltip: Gross CO₂-eq. emissions from deforestation, estimated from the loss of above- and below-ground biomass (excluding soil carbon) from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Carbon stocks were converted to CO₂-eq. by multiplying by 3.67. Note that values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.long_description: Gross (greenhouse gas) emissions from territorial deforestation (tonnes of CO2-eq) were calculated by estimating the maximum CO2-eq potentially emitted due to the full removal of the biomass as a result of territorial deforestation, estimated in a given year. This metric is calculated by multiplying the area of territorial deforestation by an estimate of the carbon stock contained in each hectare of converted land. Carbon stocks represent the total carbon stored in above- and below-ground biomass, but does not include carbon stocks in the soil. We create local estimates of biomass density (carbon stocks per hectare) using data from (Soto-Navarro et al., 2020). Carbon is converted into CO₂-eq emissions by multiplying by a factor of 44/12 ( or 3.67), based on the ratio between the molecular weight of C and CO₂ following (Pachauri et al., 2015).
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.data_source: (Pachauri et al., 2015; Soto-Navarro et al., 2020; Vancutsem C. et al., 2020)
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_DEFORESTATION_15_YEARS_TOTAL.tooltip: Cocoa deforestation is the amount of deforestation within a 15-year allocation period that is converted to cocoa plantations. To calculate it, we overlapped the cocoa area map from (Kalischek et al., 2023) (representing cocoa plantations in 2019 to 2021) with the annual loss of undisturbed Tropical Moist Forests from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021), applying a four-year lag between deforestation and first potential harvest to reflect the time from planting to harvest. Note that this does not account for cocoa expansion after 2021, and values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
COCOA_DEFORESTATION_15_YEARS_TOTAL.long_description: This metric estimates the amount of undisturbed forest converted to cocoa plantations over a 15 year period that is associated with cocoa production and exports in a selected year and department (Renier et al., 2023; Vancutsem et al., 2021). To estimate the deforestation associated with cocoa exports in a given year, we apply: a) a four-year lag between cocoa planting and the first harvest, reflecting the time required for plantations to become productive, and b) a 15-year allocation period over which plantations may contribute to traded cocoa volumes. Cocoa deforestation in 2021 is therefore calculated as the area of undisturbed forest converted to cocoa plantations between 2002 and 2017 at the location of cocoa production (Kalischek et al., 2023).
COCOA_DEFORESTATION_15_YEARS_TOTAL.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_DEFORESTATION_ANNUAL.tooltip: Annual deforestation embedded in cocoa harvest represents the area of forest loss associated with cocoa harvested in the current year, accounting for a four-year lag between land clearing and production.
COCOA_DEFORESTATION_ANNUAL.long_description: This metric estimates the annual amount of undisturbed forest converted to cocoa plantations that is associated with cocoa production and exports in a selected year and department (Renier et al., 2023; Vancutsem et al., 2021). To estimate the deforestation associated with cocoa exports in a given year, we apply a four-year lag between cocoa planting and the first harvest, reflecting the time required for plantations to become productive. Cocoa deforestation in 2021 is therefore calculated as the area of undisturbed forest converted to cocoa plantations in 2017 at the location of cocoa production (Kalischek et al., 2023).
COCOA_DEFORESTATION_ANNUAL.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

A commitment is accepted as zero deforestation if an exporter group explicitly uses the phrases 'zero deforestation', 'zero conversion' in its sustainability goals, current policies, or if they have a policy (or target) for 100% certification where the certification is equivalent to a zero-deforestation standard. \nCommitments are reported as 'company commitment' (if the specific company has a ZDC), 'none' (if the company does not have one), or 'unknown' (if the company's ZDC position was not checked).
ZDC_TRADED_COTE_DIVOIRE_COCOA_PERC.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_TN.tooltip: Estimated production of cocoa based on national production data, cocoa areas, and cocoa suitability. Cocoa areas are from (Kalischek et al., 2023), based on satellite observations from 2019 to 2021.
COCOA_TN.long_description: This metric represents the estimated volume of cocoa production per department in Côte d'Ivoire in tonnes (t) per year. Department level cocoa production was calculated based on national production statistics, derived from the International Cocoa Organization (ICCO, 2023) and allocated to the individual departments weighted based on the cocoa area (see above) and relative cocoa suitability (Schroth et al., 2016) of plantations (Kalischek et al., 2023). Note, only the total cocoa production from ICCO varied between 2019 to 2022, while cocoa area and suitability were assumed stable for the whole period.
COCOA_TN.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_AREA.tooltip: Area of land used to grow cocoa from (Kalischek et al., 2023), based on satellite observations from 2019 to 2021.
COCOA_AREA.long_description: This metric represents the area of cocoa plantations in hectares (ha) for the years 2019–2021 per department in Côte d'Ivoire based on cocoa farming maps at 10 metre resolution. Cocoa maps were obtained from (Kalischek et al., 2023) and  based on Sentinel-2 images taken between January 2019 and December 2021. Because this dataset was based on images taken in a three year time span, Trase distributes the same cocoa area in all years, from 2019 to 2021.
COCOA_AREA.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_YIELD.tooltip: Average cocoa yield combining cocoa production (annual) and the cocoa area map from (Kalischek et al., 2023) (representing cocoa plantation in 2019 to 2021).
COCOA_YIELD.long_description: Cocoa yield per department was calculated based on cocoa area and cocoa production as tonnes produced per hectare (t/ha).
COCOA_YIELD.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

TERRITORIAL_DEFORESTATION.tooltip: Deforestation of undisturbed Tropical Moist Forest derived from EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Note that values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
TERRITORIAL_DEFORESTATION.long_description: Deforestation maps were derived from the European Commission's Joint Research Centre 's TMF dataset Version 1 from 2023 (Vancutsem et al., 2021) using 41 years of Landsat time series at 30 metre spatial resolution and aggregated at department level. Deforestation refers to the year of change in land cover, from undisturbed or degraded forest (see above) to non-forest (Vancutsem et al., 2021).
TERRITORIAL_DEFORESTATION.data_source: JRC Tropical Moist Forest (AnnualChanges layer)\n(Vancutsem et al., 2021)
TERRITORIAL_DEFORESTATION.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

TERRITORIAL_DEGRADATION.tooltip: Degradation of Tropical Moist Forest derived from EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Note that values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
TERRITORIAL_DEGRADATION.long_description: Maps of degraded forest were derived from the European Commission's Joint Research Centre's TMF dataset Version 1 from 2023  (Vancutsem et al., 2021) using 41 years of Landsat time series at 30 metre spatial resolution and aggregated at department level. Forest degradation was defined as a disturbance in the tree cover canopy  visible from space over a short time period (< 2.5 years). A 'forest degradation' pixel remains forested land; i.e.,  covered by existing or regrowing trees, whereas a 'deforestation' pixel leads to the long-term (visible > 2.5 years) conversion into non-forested land  (Vancutsem et al., 2021).
TERRITORIAL_DEGRADATION.data_source: JRC Tropical Moist Forest (AnnualChanges layer)\n(Vancutsem et al., 2021)
TERRITORIAL_DEGRADATION.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

TERRITORIAL_UNDISTURBED_FOREST.tooltip: Area of undisturbed Tropical Moist Forest derived from EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Note that values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
TERRITORIAL_UNDISTURBED_FOREST.long_description: Undisturbed forest maps were derived from the European Commission's Joint Research Centre's forest cover change in tropical moist forests (TMF) dataset Version 1 from 2023 (Vancutsem et al., 2021) using 41 years of Landsat time series at 30 metre spatial resolution and aggregated at department level. Undisturbed forest was defined as a closed evergreen or semi-evergreen forest without any disturbance observed over the full Landsat historical dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021).
TERRITORIAL_UNDISTURBED_FOREST.data_source: JRC Tropical Moist Forest (AnnualChanges layer)\n(Vancutsem et al., 2021)
TERRITORIAL_UNDISTURBED_FOREST.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.display_name: Gross greenhouse gas emissions from deforestation
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.tooltip: Gross CO₂-eq. emissions from deforestation, estimated from the loss of above- and below-ground biomass (excluding soil carbon) from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Carbon stocks were converted to CO₂-eq. by multiplying by 3.67. Note that values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.long_description: Gross (greenhouse gas) emissions from territorial deforestation (tonnes of CO2-eq) were calculated by estimating the maximum CO2-eq potentially emitted due to the full removal of the biomass as a result of territorial deforestation, estimated in a given year. This metric is calculated by multiplying the area of territorial deforestation by an estimate of the carbon stock contained in each hectare of converted land. Carbon stocks represent the total carbon stored in above- and below-ground biomass, but does not include carbon stocks in the soil. We create local estimates of biomass density (carbon stocks per hectare) using data from (Soto-Navarro et al., 2020). Carbon is converted into CO₂-eq emissions by multiplying by a factor of 44/12 ( or 3.67), based on the ratio between the molecular weight of C and CO₂ following (Pachauri et al., 2015).
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.data_source: (Pachauri et al., 2015; Soto-Navarro et al., 2020; Vancutsem C. et al., 2020)
CO2_GROSS_EMISSIONS_TERRITORIAL_DEFOREST.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_DEFORESTATION_15_YEARS_TOTAL.tooltip: Cocoa deforestation is the amount of deforestation within a 15-year allocation period that is converted to cocoa plantations. To calculate it, we overlapped the cocoa area map from (Kalischek et al., 2023) (representing cocoa plantations in 2019 to 2021) with the annual loss of undisturbed Tropical Moist Forests from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021), applying a four-year lag between deforestation and first potential harvest to reflect the time from planting to harvest. Note that this does not account for cocoa expansion after 2021, and values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
COCOA_DEFORESTATION_15_YEARS_TOTAL.long_description: This metric estimates the amount of undisturbed forest converted to cocoa plantations over a 15 year period that is associated with cocoa production and exports in a selected year and department (Renier et al., 2023; Vancutsem et al., 2021). To estimate the deforestation associated with cocoa exports in a given year, we apply: a) a four-year lag between cocoa planting and the first harvest, reflecting the time required for plantations to become productive, and b) a 15-year allocation period over which plantations may contribute to traded cocoa volumes. Cocoa deforestation in 2021 is therefore calculated as the area of undisturbed forest converted to cocoa plantations between 2002 and 2017 at the location of cocoa production (Kalischek et al., 2023).
COCOA_DEFORESTATION_15_YEARS_TOTAL.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_DEFORESTATION_ANNUAL.tooltip: Annual deforestation embedded in cocoa harvest represents the area of forest loss associated with cocoa harvested in the current year, accounting for a four-year lag between land clearing and production.
COCOA_DEFORESTATION_ANNUAL.long_description: This metric estimates the annual amount of undisturbed forest converted to cocoa plantations that is associated with cocoa production and exports in a selected year and department (Renier et al., 2023; Vancutsem et al., 2021). To estimate the deforestation associated with cocoa exports in a given year, we apply a four-year lag between cocoa planting and the first harvest, reflecting the time required for plantations to become productive. Cocoa deforestation in 2021 is therefore calculated as the area of undisturbed forest converted to cocoa plantations in 2017 at the location of cocoa production (Kalischek et al., 2023).
COCOA_DEFORESTATION_ANNUAL.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_15_YEARS_TOTAL.tooltip: Gross CO₂-equivalent emissions from cocoa deforestation (15-year allocation period, 4-year lag), estimated from the loss of above- and below-ground biomass (excluding soil carbon). Carbon stocks were converted to CO₂-equivalent by multiplying by 3.67. To calculate above and belowground biomass loss, we overlapped the cocoa area map from (Kalischek et al., 2023) (representing cocoa plantations in 2019 to 2021) with the loss of undisturbed Tropical Moist Forests from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021), applying a four-year lag between deforestation and first potential harvest to reflect the time from planting to harvest. Note that values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_15_YEARS_TOTAL.long_description: This metric estimates the gross greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions associated with cocoa-driven deforestation over a 15-year period expressed in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent, and embedded in cocoa trade.  Emissions are calculated from the carbon stored in above- and below-ground biomass lost when undisturbed forest is deforested (excl. degradation) (Vancutsem et al., 2021) and converted to cocoa plantations (Kalischek et al., 2023), excluding soil carbon. To link emissions to cocoa exports, the metric applies a four-year lag between deforestation and the first cocoa harvest, reflecting the time required for cocoa trees to become productive, and allocates impacts over a 15-year production period. Carbon stock estimates are based on local biomass density data (Soto-Navarro et al., 2020) and converted to CO₂-equivalent using a factor of 3.67 (Pachauri et al., 2015). Estimates are based on cocoa plantation maps (Kalischek et al., 2023) and tropical forest loss data from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Values for recent years may change in future dataset updates as recent forest disturbance is reclassified over time.
COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_15_YEARS_TOTAL.data_source: (Kalischek et al., 2023; Pachauri et al., 2015; Soto-Navarro et al., 2020; Vancutsem et al., 2021)
COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_15_YEARS_TOTAL.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_ANNUAL.display_name: Gross emissions from annual cocoa deforestation
COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_ANNUAL.tooltip: Annual gross CO₂-equivalent emissions embedded in cocoa harvest were estimated from the loss of above- and below-ground biomass (excluding soil carbon). Carbon stocks were converted to CO₂-equivalent by multiplying by 3.67. To calculate above and belowground biomass loss, we overlapped the cocoa area map from (Kalischek et al., 2023) (representing cocoa plantations in 2019 to 2021) with the annual loss of undisturbed Tropical Moist Forests from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021).
COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_ANNUAL.long_description: This metric estimates the annual gross greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions associated with cocoa-driven deforestation expressed in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent and embedded in cocoa trade. Emissions are calculated from the carbon stored in above- and below-ground biomass lost when undisturbed forest is deforested (excl. degradation) (Vancutsem et al., 2021) and converted to cocoa plantations (Kalischek et al., 2023), excluding soil carbon. To link emissions to cocoa exports, the metric applies a four-year lag between deforestation and the first cocoa harvest, reflecting the time required for cocoa trees to become productive. Carbon stock estimates are based on local biomass density data (Soto-Navarro et al., 2020) and converted to CO₂-equivalent using a factor of 3.67 (Pachauri et al., 2015). Estimates are based on cocoa plantation maps  (Kalischek et al., 2023) and tropical forest loss data from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Values for recent years may change in future dataset updates as recent forest disturbance is reclassified over time.
COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_ANNUAL.data_source: (Kalischek et al., 2023; Pachauri et al., 2015; Soto-Navarro et al., 2020; Vancutsem et al., 2021)
COCOA_GROSS_EMISSIONS_ANNUAL.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_NET_EMISSIONS_15_YEARS_TOTAL.tooltip: Net greenhouse gas emissions from cocoa deforestation (15-year allocation period, 4-year lag), were calculated as the difference between gross emissions from cocoa deforestation and sequestration in new cocoa plantations. To calculate above and belowground biomass loss, we overlapped the cocoa area map from (Kalischek et al., 2023) (representing cocoa plantations in 2019 to 2021) with the loss of undisturbed Tropical Moist Forests from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021), applying a four-year lag between deforestation and first potential harvest to reflect the time from planting to harvest. Note that values for the most recent 2 years may change in the future when new versions of the Tropical Moist Forest dataset are released, updated to reflect whether recent forest change shows temporary degradation or permanent deforestation.
COCOA_NET_EMISSIONS_15_YEARS_TOTAL.long_description: This metric estimates the net greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions associated with cocoa-driven deforestation over a 15-year period expressed in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent, and embedded in cocoa trade. Net emissions are calculated as the difference between gross emissions from the loss of above- and below-ground biomass in undisturbed forests converted to cocoa plantations and carbon sequestration in cocoa and shade trees (Vervuurt et al., 2022), excluding soil carbon and forest degradation. To link emissions to cocoa exports, the metric applies a four-year lag between deforestation and the first cocoa harvest, and allocates impacts over a 15-year production period. Estimates are based on cocoa plantation maps (Kalischek et al., 2023) and tropical forest loss data from the EC JRC Tropical Moist Forest dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021). Values for recent years may change in future dataset updates as recent forest disturbance is reclassified over time.
COCOA_NET_EMISSIONS_15_YEARS_TOTAL.data_source: (Kalischek et al., 2023; Soto-Navarro et al., 2020; Vancutsem et al., 2021; Vervuurt et al., 2022)
COCOA_NET_EMISSIONS_15_YEARS_TOTAL.citation: French, N., Guye, V., Gollnow, F., Biddle, H., Ribeiro, V., Meyfroidt, P., Renier, C., & zu Ermgassen, E. K. H. J. (2026). Côte d’Ivoire cocoa supply chain v.1.2 (2022-2024) (Version 1.2) [Data set]. Trase.

COCOA_NET_EMISSIONS_ANNUAL.display_name: Net emissions from annual cocoa deforestation

TERRITORIAL_UNDISTURBED_FOREST.long_description: Undisturbed forest maps were derived from the European Commission's Joint Research Centre's forest cover change in tropical moist forests (TMF) dataset Version 1 from 2023 (Vancutsem et al., 2021) using 41 years of Landsat time series at 30 metre spatial resolution and aggregated at department level. Undisturbed forest was defined as a closed evergreen or semi-evergreen forest without any disturbance observed over the full Landsat historical dataset (Vancutsem et al., 2021).
TERRITORIAL_UNDISTURBED_FOREST.data_source: JRC Tropical Moist Forest (AnnualChanges layer)\n(Vancutsem et al., 2021)
